posts.title: Li Auto kicks off European push with golf partnership, names overseas i6 Li 6
posts.summary:
Li Auto confirmed that the Li i6 will appear as the Li 6 at next month's Paris Motor Show, where it will unveil its global product lineup and European business plans.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto has officially initiated its European market entry, utilizing the 2026 Solheim Cup in the Netherlands as a platform to showcase its Li i6 electric SUV.
The company confirmed that the Li i6 will be rebranded as the 'Li 6' for international markets, with a formal debut scheduled for the Paris Motor Show in October.
Li Auto's European strategy prioritizes battery electric vehicles (BEVs), distinguishing it from the company's focus on extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs) in the Middle East and Central Asia.
While specific European pricing and distribution channels remain undisclosed, the company plans to commence sales of the Li 6 in the region during the fourth quarter of 2026.

posts.title: Geely launches Galaxy TT sedan with lower starting price, longer range
posts.summary:
The Geely Galaxy TT starts at a limited-time price of 129,900 yuan ($19,170), with CLTC ranges of 640-725 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely launched the Galaxy TT electric sedan with a competitive starting price of 129,900 yuan, marking an 11% reduction from its pre-sale pricing.
The vehicle lineup features an 800-volt high-voltage architecture and CATL's Shenxing LFP batteries, enabling 6C fast charging across all variants.
Performance specifications include a 0-100 km/h acceleration time of 3.8 seconds for the dual-motor Ultra variant and a maximum CLTC range of 725 km for the flagship rear-wheel-drive model.
The sedan incorporates advanced hardware, including LiDAR-based driver assistance systems on most trims and a sophisticated suspension setup designed to enhance sporty handling.

posts.title: Powering AI is an architecture problem
posts.summary: On July 22, 2026, a transmission line fault in Ashburn, Virginia—the heart of the world’s largest data center cluster—knocked more than 3 gigawatts of load off the grid in seconds. And it wasn’t the first time. Two years earlier, a single failed surge arrester dropped roughly 60 Virginia facilities and 1,500 megawatts at once. No…
bullets: Recent grid failures in Ashburn, Virginia, demonstrate that data center power issues are increasingly architectural rather than just supply-side constraints.
AI data centers create extreme volatility by swinging up to 70% of their load in milliseconds, a behavior pattern the legacy power grid was never designed to accommodate.
Standard data center power stacks are failing because current UPS systems are designed for short-term backup rather than absorbing high-frequency, gigawatt-scale load fluctuations.

The industry's reliance on 'eco-mode' bypass configurations leaves compute infrastructure vulnerable to grid transients and prevents effective filtering of the massive load swings generated by AI training.

posts.title: Redefining Processes At Sub-2nm
posts.summary:
Discrete steps are being merged with others as dimensions shrink into the angstrom range.
The post Redefining Processes At Sub-2nm appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Manufacturing at sub-2nm nodes is forcing the integration of previously discrete process steps as shrinking dimensions eliminate the margin for error.

Extreme structural fragility at the angstrom scale means traditional wafer probing can damage oxide layers or hybrid bonds, leading manufacturers to adopt sacrificial pads and pre-test bonding strategies.
The shift toward chiplet-based architectures to overcome reticle size limits introduces new challenges in thermal density and structural stress that complicate traditional manufacturing workflows.
Large-scale AI data centers are shifting their strategy toward system-level redundancy to mitigate the inevitable manufacturing defects inherent in these highly complex, multi-die configurations.

posts.title: Silent Data Errors Redefine Test Coverage And Fleet Maintenance Strategies
posts.summary:
Through better manufacturing screening, DFT for systems and fleet monitors, this major scourge on data center hardware is gradually being tamed.
The post Silent Data Errors Redefine Test Coverage And Fleet Maintenance Strategies appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Silent Data Errors (SDEs) are becoming a critical threat to AI infrastructure, with failure rates that scale to an incident every four days in a fleet of 10 million devices even at low FIT levels.
The industry is pivoting from traditional commercial reliability standards of 100-300 DPPM toward automotive-grade requirements of sub-1 DPPM to address the risks posed by advanced node chiplets.

SDEs represent a significant financial risk, as subtle manufacturing defects can trigger data corruption or service outages that result in billions of dollars in potential losses for data center operators.

Engineers are increasingly relying on enhanced Design-for-Test (DFT) and fleet-wide monitoring to detect stealth defects that escape initial manufacturing screens and manifest only under high-utilization workloads.
